title: Pontryagin Duality for Locally Compact Abelian Groups

items.title: Compact-open neighbourhoods on the dual give a neighbourhood basis on the group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group with dual $\widehat G$ ([[def-pontryagin-dual-and-compact-open-topology]]). For $x_1\in G$, compact $K\subseteq\widehat G$ and $\epsilon>0$ put $$N_{x_1}(K,\epsilon):=\{x\in G:|\chi(x)-\chi(x_1)|<\epsilon\ \text{for all}\ \chi\in K\}.$$ Then every $N_{x_1}(K,\epsilon)$ is open in $G$, and these sets form a neighbourhood basis at $x_1$. Consequently the evaluation map $\Phi:G\to\widehat{\widehat G}$, $\Phi(x)(\chi):=\chi(x)$, is a homeomorphism onto its image, and $G$ carries the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $\widehat G$.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Lemma 13.1, printed p. 26: uniform-on-dual-compact sets are open and form neighbourhood bases on the original LCA group.

items.strategy: Compact evaluation maxima and joint continuity make uniform-on-compact neighbourhoods open, with the empty compact handled separately. For each open identity neighbourhood U, construct a nonnegative compactly supported g whose support difference lies in U. Its convolution square f has positive f(0), an integrable nonnegative transform, and pointwise inversion. A compact transform tail and a sufficiently small uniform error ensure |f(x)-f(0)|<f(0)/2 on one dual-compact neighbourhood, hence that neighbourhood lies in U. Translation gives the full basis. Joint evaluation proves continuity into the bidual, and the proved basis plus character separation gives a topological embedding.

items.title: Compactly supported nonnegative transform bumps on the dual
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group with dual $\widehat G$ and Haar measure $m_G$, let $\gamma_0\in\widehat G$ and let $K\subseteq\widehat G$ be a compact neighbourhood of $\gamma_0$. Then there exists $f\in L^1(G,m_G)$ with $\widehat f\ge0$ on $\widehat G$, $\widehat f(\gamma_0)>0$ and $\widehat f=0$ on $\widehat G\setminus K$.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Lemma 13.2, printed p. 26: a nonnegative transform positive at a chosen character and vanishing outside a compact neighbourhood.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Section 36D, regularity corollary and its proof, printed p. 146: inverse square-integrable transforms give local transform cutoffs.

items.strategy: Given a compact neighborhood K of γ₀ in Ghat, choose a relatively compact open symmetric identity neighborhood V with γ₀ Vbar Vbar⁻¹ contained in K. In L²(Ghat), let a=1_V and b=1_(γ₀⁻¹V). Full Plancherel on G gives u,v∈L²(G) with F_Gu=a and F_Gv=b. Set f=u·conjugate(v)∈L¹(G) by Cauchy–Schwarz. For ω∈Ghat, modulation and Plancherel give F_Gf(ω)=<u,ωv>=∫_Ghat a(χ)conjugate(b(ω⁻¹χ))dm_Ghat(χ)=m_Ghat(V∩ωγ₀⁻¹V). This overlap is nonnegative, equals m_Ghat(V)>0 at γ₀, and vanishes unless ω∈γ₀VV⁻¹. Translation continuity makes the transform continuous, so its support is contained in γ₀ Vbar Vbar⁻¹⊂K. The modulation identity extends from C_c(G) to L²(G) by density and continuity of the unitary operators. This proof uses Plancherel before biduality and has no biduality dependency.

items.title: A locally compact subgroup of a Hausdorff topological group is closed
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a Hausdorff topological group ([[def-hausdorff-space]], [[def-topological-group]]) and let $H\le G$ be a subgroup ([[def-subgroup]]) which is locally compact in the subspace topology ([[def-subspace-topology-top]], [[def-locally-compact-space]]). Then $H$ is closed in $G$. Conversely, if $G$ is locally compact and $H$ is closed in $G$, then $H$ is locally compact in the subspace topology. In particular, closed subgroups of locally compact Hausdorff abelian groups are again locally compact Hausdorff abelian.

No choice principle is used.

references.title: Linus Kramer, Locally Compact Groups and Lie Groups, Chapter 1 (author lecture notes, 2020)
references.locator: Corollary 1.14 and its proof, printed p. 8; Proposition 1.29, printed p. 13: locally compact subgroups of Hausdorff groups are closed, and closed subgroups of locally compact groups are locally compact.

items.strategy: Choose an H-open identity neighbourhood V with compact relative closure C and write V=H∩O for ambient open O. The compact C is ambient closed, so closure_G(V)⊆C⊆H. For x in closure_G(H), the open identity translate x−O meets H; write x=h+o. Then o=−h+x belongs to closure_G(H)∩O⊆closure_G(H∩O)⊆C, so x belongs to H. Conversely, if H is closed and G locally compact, compact ambient neighbourhoods intersect H in compact relative neighbourhoods; operations and Hausdorffness restrict, giving the LCA subgroup assertion.

items.title: The quotient of an LCA group by a closed subgroup is LCA
items.statement: Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian topological group ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]], [[def-topological-group]]) and let $H\le G$ be a closed subgroup ([[def-subgroup]]). Then the quotient group $G/H$ with the quotient topology ([[def-quotient-group]], [[def-quotient-topology]]) is a locally compact Hausdorff abelian topological group. No choice principle is used.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Section 28C, theorem and Corollary 1, printed p. 111: quotient projections are open and quotients are locally compact.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Lemmas 3.1 and 3.7, printed pp. 7-8: quotient group operations and the Hausdorff property for closed normal subgroups.

items.title: Pontryagin biduality: the evaluation map is a topological isomorphism
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group with dual $\widehat G$ and bidual $\widehat{\widehat G}$. Then $$\Phi:G\to\widehat{\widehat G},\qquad \Phi(x)(\gamma):=\gamma(x),$$ is an isomorphism of topological groups.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Section 37D, printed pp. 151-152: the evaluation map is an isomorphism and a homeomorphism onto the bidual.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Theorem 13.3, printed p. 26: Pontryagin biduality.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, Theorem C.12, printed p. 437: Pontryagin duality. Theorem C.13 is the subsequent subgroup calculus.

items.strategy: Let Φ(x)(γ)=γ(x). It is a homomorphism, continuous by the compact-open dual topology, and injective because continuous characters separate points. The neighborhood-basis lemma for compact subsets of Ĝ shows that Φ is a homeomorphism onto its image. Since G is locally compact and Ĝ̂ is Hausdorff, its image is a locally compact subgroup and is closed. If the image were proper, choose ξ₀ outside it and a compact neighborhood K⊂Ĝ̂ disjoint from the image. Apply [[lem-positive-compactly-supported-transform-bump-on-the-dual]] to the LCA group Ĝ: obtain f∈L¹(Ĝ) whose transform is supported in K and is positive at ξ₀. The finite complex measure μ=f m_Ĝ is regular: choose h_n∈C_c(Ĝ) with h_n→f in L¹; each h_n m_Ĝ is finite regular, and ||(f−h_n)m_Ĝ||_TV=||f−h_n||₁→0. Finite regular complex measures are closed in total-variation norm, since compact and open approximations for each Borel set transfer from an approximant with the total-variation distance bounding the error. For every x∈G its inverse Fourier–Stieltjes transform is ∫_Ĝ γ(x)dμ(γ)=F_Ĝ f(Φ(−x))=0, because Φ(−x) lies in the image and the transform is supported in K. Fourier–Stieltjes uniqueness implies μ=0, so f=0 almost everywhere and its Fourier transform vanishes at ξ₀, contradicting positivity. Therefore the closed image is all of Ĝ̂, and Φ is the asserted topological isomorphism.

items.title: Continuous characters separate points of an LCA group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]], [[def-topological-group]]) and let $x\in G$ with $x\ne0$. Then there is $\gamma\in\widehat G$ with $\gamma(x)\ne1$. Equivalently, the evaluation map $\Phi(x)(\gamma):=\gamma(x)$ is injective on $G$.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Section 36A, printed pp. 141-142: Bochner representation; Section 36B, printed p. 142: convolution squares and the positive-definite core. The separating bump argument is supplied here.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Theorem 13.3, printed p. 26: injectivity of the evaluation map; the independent Bochner proof is supplied here.

items.strategy: Choose a compact symmetric identity neighbourhood $S$ with $(S+S^{-1})\cap(x+S+S^{-1})=\emptyset$ (Hausdorffness and continuity of subtraction), pick $g\in C_c(G)$, $g\ge0$, $g\not\equiv0$, supported in $S$, and set $h:=g*\widetilde g$. Then $h\in C_c(G)$ is continuous positive definite, $h(0)=\|g\|_2^2>0$ and $h(x)=0$ because $\operatorname{supp}g\cap(x+\operatorname{supp}g)=\emptyset$. By Bochner's theorem ([[thm-bochner-theorem-for-lca-groups]]) $h=\widehat\mu$ for a finite positive measure $\mu$ on $\widehat G$ of mass $h(0)$. If $\gamma(x)=1$ for all $\gamma\in\widehat G$, then $h(x)=\int_{\widehat G}\gamma(x)\,d\mu(\gamma)=\mu(\widehat G)=h(0)$, contradicting $h(x)=0$.

items.title: The annihilator of a subgroup
items.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian topological group with dual $\widehat G$ and let $H\le G$ be a subgroup. The **annihilator** of $H$ is
$$H^\perp:=\{\gamma\in\widehat G:\gamma(h)=1\ \text{for every}\ h\in H\}.$$
It is a subgroup of $\widehat G$, equal to the kernel of the restriction homomorphism $\widehat G\to\widehat H$, $\gamma\mapsto\gamma|_H$; if $H$ is closed in $G$ it is a closed subgroup of $\widehat G$. The annihilator of a subgroup $L\le\widehat G$ is written $L^\perp:=\{x\in G:\lambda(x)=1\ \text{for all}\ \lambda\in L\}$ when the bidual identification $G\cong\widehat{\widehat G}$ of [[thm-pontryagin-biduality]] is in force, and the convention $(H)^\perp=(\overline H)^\perp$ is recorded: a character is trivial on $H$ exactly when it is trivial on the closure of $H$.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Definition 14.1 and Lemma 14.2(i), printed p. 27: the annihilator and its closedness.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, Theorem C.13, printed p. 437: the closed-subgroup annihilator and quotient-dual identifications; the extension to arbitrary subgroups is established in the definition here.

items.strategy: Definition row; no proof obligation. The only verifications are that $H^\perp$ is a subgroup (pointwise products of characters trivial on $H$ are trivial on $H$), that $H^\perp=\ker(\gamma\mapsto\gamma|_H)$ by definition, and that a kernel of a continuous homomorphism between Hausdorff groups is closed.

items.title: The dual of a quotient is the annihilator
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group and let $H\le G$ be a closed subgroup. Then the pullback of the quotient homomorphism $q:G\to G/H$, $$\widehat q:\widehat{G/H}\to\widehat G,\qquad \widehat q(\chi):=\chi\circ q,$$ is an isomorphism of topological groups onto the annihilator $H^\perp$ ([[def-annihilator-of-a-subgroup]]), which is therefore a closed subgroup of $\widehat G$ topologically isomorphic to $\widehat{G/H}$. The Axiom of Choice is used exactly as in the published compact-lift theorem for closed-subgroup quotients quoted below, and in no other place.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Section 35B, printed p. 139: the topological quotient-dual identification.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Lemma 14.2(iii), printed p. 27: the quotient dual is the annihilator.

items.strategy: This row re-presents, at the page's stable ID, the exactness statement already proved in the published library item [[lem-dual-homomorphisms-are-continuous-and-functorial]] part (b), whose statement reads: for a closed subgroup $H$ of a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group $G$, $\widehat q:\widehat{G/H}\to\widehat G$ is a topological group isomorphism onto $H^\perp$. No new proof is minted: the strategy is to cite that published result together with the definition of the annihilator; the AC use is exactly the published item's compact-lift theorem for closed subgroup quotients. The batch notes record that this is an intentional interface re-presentation of a published supplier, not a new claim.

items.title: Annihilators reverse inclusions and the double annihilator closes the subgroup
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group with dual $\widehat G$ and bidual identification $G\cong\widehat{\widehat G}$ of [[thm-pontryagin-biduality]].

(1) If $H\le K\le G$ then $K^\perp\le H^\perp$.

(2) For every subgroup $H\le G$ one has $(H^\perp)^\perp=\overline H$; in particular $H\subseteq(H^\perp)^\perp$ and the double annihilator is closed.

(3) For a closed subgroup $H\le G$ this reads $H^{\perp\perp}=H$.

The same statements hold with the roles of $G$ and $\widehat G$ exchanged, annihilators of subgroups of $\widehat G$ being computed in $\widehat{\widehat G}\cong G$.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Lemma 14.2(ii), printed p. 27: the double annihilator of a closed subgroup equals the subgroup; the closure case and inclusion reversal are proved here.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, Theorem C.13, printed p. 437: the closed-subgroup double-annihilator identity.

items.strategy:
Part (1) is immediate from the definitions. For (2), $H^\perp=(\overline H)^\perp$ by density of $H$ and continuity of characters, so assume $H$ closed. Then $H^{\perp\perp}\supseteq H$, and if $x
otin H$ the quotient $G/H$ is a nontrivial locally compact abelian group, so some character of $G/H$ is nontrivial at $x+H$ ([[lem-continuous-characters-separate-points-of-an-lca-group]] applied to $G/H$, which is locally compact abelian by [[lem-dual-homomorphisms-are-continuous-and-functorial]]); pulling it back along the quotient map via the quotient universal property and [[thm-pontryagin-dual-of-an-lca-quotient-is-the-annihilator]] gives $\gamma\in H^\perp$ with $\gamma(x)
e1$, so $x
otin H^{\perp\perp}$. Part (3) is (2) for closed $H$. The exchange of roles uses [[thm-pontryagin-biduality]] applied to $\widehat G$.

items.title: Characters of a closed subgroup extend to the ambient LCA group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group and let $H\le G$ be a closed subgroup. Then the restriction homomorphism $$R:\widehat G\to\widehat H,\qquad R(\gamma):=\gamma|_H,$$ is surjective: every continuous character of $H$ extends to a continuous character of $G$.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Theorem 14.3, printed p. 27: every character of a closed subgroup extends to the ambient LCA group.

items.strategy: Set $L:=R(\widehat G)\le\widehat H$ and use the annihilator calculus of [[lem-annihilator-reverses-inclusion-and-double-annihilator-closes]] inside the locally compact abelian group $\widehat H$, with $\widehat{\widehat H}\cong H$ supplied by [[thm-pontryagin-biduality]]. First, $L^\perp=\{h\in H:\gamma(h)=1\ \text{for all}\ \gamma\in\widehat G\}=\{0\}$ by [[lem-continuous-characters-separate-points-of-an-lca-group]] for $G$, so $\overline L=(L^\perp)^\perp=\{0\}^\perp=\widehat H$: $L$ is dense. Second, $R$ factors as $\widehat G\to\widehat G/H^\perp\to\widehat H$, the first map being the quotient homomorphism and the second a continuous injective homomorphism $\psi$ with image $L$; by [[thm-pontryagin-dual-of-an-lca-quotient-is-the-annihilator]] and [[lem-annihilator-reverses-inclusion-and-double-annihilator-closes]], the transpose of $\psi$ is the identity of $H$ under the bidual identifications, so $\psi$ is a homeomorphism onto its image (functoriality of duals, naturality of evaluation, and [[thm-pontryagin-biduality]] for $\widehat G/H^\perp$ and $\widehat H$). Hence $L\cong\widehat G/H^\perp$ is locally compact, so $L$ is closed in $\widehat H$ by [[lem-local-compact-subgroups-of-hausdorff-groups-are-closed]]. Dense and closed give $L=\widehat H$.

items.title: The dual of a closed subgroup is a quotient of the dual
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group with dual $\widehat G$ and let $H\le G$ be a closed subgroup. Then restriction $$R:\widehat G\to\widehat H,\qquad R(\gamma):=\gamma|_H,$$ is an open continuous surjection with kernel $H^\perp$ ([[def-annihilator-of-a-subgroup]]), and it induces an isomorphism of topological groups $$\widehat G/H^\perp\;\cong\;\widehat H .$$

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Lemma 14.2(iv), printed p. 27: the dual of a closed subgroup is the quotient of the dual by its annihilator.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, Theorem C.13, second bullet, printed p. 437: the closed-subgroup dual is the dual quotient.

items.strategy: Surjectivity is [[lem-character-extension-from-a-closed-subgroup-of-an-lca-group]]; continuity is functoriality of duals, and the kernel is $H^\perp$ by definition ([[def-annihilator-of-a-subgroup]]). The induced continuous bijection $\psi:\widehat G/H^\perp\to\widehat H$ is a homeomorphism: the same transpose computation as in the extension lemma identifies $\widehat\psi$ with the identity of $H$ between the bidual identifications, so $\psi$ is a homeomorphism onto its image by naturality of evaluation and [[thm-pontryagin-biduality]] applied to $\widehat G/H^\perp$ and $\widehat H$; alternatively one concludes openness of $R$ from this homeomorphism and the quotient universal property.

items.title: The Plancherel transform range is dense in L^2 of the dual
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice
([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian
group and let $\mathcal F:L^2(G,m_G)\to L^2(\widehat G,m_{\widehat G})$ be the
isometric extension of the Fourier transform on $L^1\cap L^2$ with respect to
the compatible dual Haar normalisation. Then $\mathcal F$ has dense range;
equivalently, every $q\in L^2(\widehat G)$ orthogonal to $\mathcal F(L^2(G))$
is zero.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Section 36D, printed pp. 145-146: completion of the isometry to a unitary transform, including dense range before the biduality theorem. The Fourier-Stieltjes uniqueness proof here is an altered route.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, printed p. 435, paragraph preceding Theorem C.8: the transform on the integrable square-integrable intersection has dense range and extends surjectively.

items.strategy: Let T be the FR-16 isometric extension, and suppose q∈L²(Ĝ) is orthogonal to T(L²(G)). For every f∈L¹(G)∩L²(G), the extension agrees with the L¹ Fourier transform, and the translation identity gives T(T_x f)(γ)=conjugate(γ(x))F_G f(γ). Put g_f=q·conjugate(F_G f)∈L¹(Ĝ) by Cauchy–Schwarz. The measure μ_f=g_f m_Ĝ is finite and regular: choose h_n∈C_c(Ĝ) with h_n→g_f in L¹; each h_n m_Ĝ is finite regular because Haar measure is Radon, and the L¹-to-total-variation formula gives ||(g_f−h_n)m_Ĝ||_TV=||g_f−h_n||₁→0. Finite regular complex measures are closed in total-variation norm: compact and open approximations for a Borel set transfer from an approximating measure, with the total-variation distance bounding the error. Thus μ_f is regular. Orthogonality and the translation formula give ∫_Ĝ γ(x)dμ_f(γ)=0 for every x∈G. Fourier–Stieltjes uniqueness yields μ_f=0, and the total-variation formula then gives g_f=0 almost everywhere. For each γ∈Ĝ choose a relatively compact open identity neighborhood U_γ on which Re(conjugate(γ))>1/2 and set f_γ=1_{U_γ}∈L¹(G)∩L²(G). Haar positivity gives Re(F_G f_γ(γ))>0; the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma makes O_γ={η∈Ĝ:F_G f_γ(η)≠0} an open neighborhood of γ. Applying the preceding conclusion to f_γ shows q=0 almost everywhere on O_γ. By C_c(Ĝ) density in L²(Ĝ), choose q_n∈C_c(Ĝ) with q_n→q in L². Each compact support supp(q_n) has a finite subcover by the O_γ, so q=0 almost everywhere on every supp(q_n). Outside their countable union all q_n vanish, and L² convergence gives q=0 almost everywhere there too. Hence q=0 in L²(Ĝ). The range of T is closed because T is an isometry and L²(G) is complete; the closed-subspace orthogonal-complement lemma now gives density, indeed surjectivity. This proof does not use biduality.

items.title: The Plancherel theorem for locally compact abelian groups
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group with Haar measure $m_G$ and dual $\widehat G$ carrying the compatible dual Haar normalisation. Then the Fourier transform extends uniquely to a unitary operator $$\mathcal F:L^2(G,m_G)\to L^2(\widehat G,m_{\widehat G}),$$ that is, $\langle\mathcal Ff,\mathcal Fg\rangle=\langle f,g\rangle$ for all $f,g\in L^2(G)$, and $\mathcal F$ is bijective.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Section 36D, printed pp. 145-146: the unitary Plancherel theorem.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, printed p. 435, paragraph preceding Theorem C.8 and Theorem C.8 (Parseval).

items.strategy: The isometric extension $\mathcal F$ exists by [[thm-lca-plancherel-isometric-extension]]. Its range is a closed subspace of $L^2(\widehat G)$: if $\mathcal F f_n\to h$, then $(f_n)$ is Cauchy in $L^2(G)$, converges to some $f$ by completeness ([[thm-riesz-fischer-completeness-of-l-p]]), and continuity of $\mathcal F$ gives $h=\mathcal F f$. The range is dense by [[lem-lca-transform-range-is-dense-in-ltwo-of-the-dual]], so it is all of $L^2(\widehat G)$; an isometric linear surjection is unitary.

items.title: Compact and discrete transforms are the two extreme Plancherel cases
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group.

(1) If $G$ is compact with $m_G(G)=1$, its dual $\widehat G$ is discrete and the compatible dual Haar measure gives each point mass $1$; the Plancherel theorem then reads as the Fourier-series identity $$\|f\|_2^2=\sum_{\gamma\in\widehat G}|\widehat f(\gamma)|^2,\qquad f\in L^2(G).$$

(2) If $G$ is discrete with $m_G$ the counting measure (each point of mass $1$), then $\widehat G$ is compact and the compatible dual Haar measure is the normalised Haar measure of $\widehat G$, and Plancherel reads $$\sum_{x\in G}|f(x)|^2=\|\widehat f\|_2^2,\qquad f\in\ell^2(G).$$

Without the stated normalisation of $m_G$ the identification of the dual measure in (2) is false; the compatible scale is reciprocal in $m_G$, as [[thm-compatible-dual-haar-normalisation]] records. For a general $L^2$ function, $\widehat f$ denotes the Plancherel transform $\mathcal Ff$; its pointwise integral formula is asserted only when $f\in L^1$.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Sections 38B-38C, printed pp. 154-155: compatible compact/discrete Haar scales and the Fourier-series Parseval identity.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, Theorem C.8, printed p. 435, and the compact/discrete normalisation discussion after Theorem C.10, printed p. 436.

items.strategy: Use the compact/discrete dual theorem. For compact G with total Haar mass 1, translation invariance gives character orthogonality and each character transforms to its singleton indicator. Plancherel fixes each dual atom at mass 1; inner regularity identifies counting measure on all subsets of the discrete dual. For discrete G with counting measure, the delta at 0 transforms to constant 1, and Plancherel fixes total dual Haar mass at 1. The general identities use the L2 extension, with integral transforms only on L1, and compatible Haar rescaling is reciprocal.

items.title: Compactness and discreteness are exchanged by duality
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group. Then:

(1) $G$ is compact if and only if $\widehat G$ is discrete;

(2) $G$ is discrete if and only if $\widehat G$ is compact.

The Axiom of Choice supplies the Tychonoff-based compactness implication and the choice hypotheses of biduality used in the converses.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Section 38A, printed pp. 153-154: compactness and discreteness are exchanged, with the converses using biduality.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, Lemma C.7, printed pp. 434-435, and Theorem C.12, printed p. 437: the forward compact/discrete implications and biduality.

items.strategy: One implication of each equivalence is the corresponding clause of the published [[thm-compact-groups-have-discrete-duals-and-discrete-groups-have-compact-duals]]. For the converse implications apply that theorem to the locally compact abelian group $\widehat G$ (which is locally compact abelian by [[thm-dual-of-an-lca-group-is-locally-compact-abelian]]) and use the biduality identification $G\cong\widehat{\widehat G}$ of [[thm-pontryagin-biduality]]: if $\widehat G$ is compact then $\widehat{\widehat G}$ is discrete, so $G$ is discrete; if $\widehat G$ is discrete then $\widehat{\widehat G}$ is compact, so $G$ is compact. The AC use is inherited from the Tychonoff-based clause (2) of the published theorem.

items.title: Biduality commutes with products, closed subgroups and quotients
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

(1) For locally compact Hausdorff abelian groups $G_1,\dots,G_n$, under the product-dual identification $\widehat{G_1\times\cdots\times G_n}\cong\widehat G_1\times\cdots\times\widehat G_n$ of [[lem-duals-of-finite-products-and-discrete-direct-sums]] one has $\Phi_{G_1\times\cdots\times G_n}=\Phi_{G_1}\times\cdots\times\Phi_{G_n}$.

(2) For a closed subgroup $H\le G$ of a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group $G$, the evaluation isomorphisms intertwine the exact sequences $0\to H\to G\to G/H\to0$ with their duals: under the identifications $\widehat H\cong\widehat G/H^\perp$ and $\widehat{G/H}\cong H^\perp$ of [[thm-dual-of-a-closed-subgroup-is-the-dual-quotient]] and [[thm-pontryagin-dual-of-an-lca-quotient-is-the-annihilator]], the restrictions of $\Phi_G$ recover $\Phi_H$ and $\Phi_{G/H}$, and $H^{\perp\perp}=H$.

(3) The analogous statements hold for finite products of closed subgroups and of quotients.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Lemmas 14.2 and 14.4, printed p. 27: quotient/subgroup duals and finite-product duality. The evaluation compatibility is computed here.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, Theorem C.13 and the homomorphism-dual paragraph following it, printed p. 437: subgroup, quotient and functorial duality.

items.strategy: Part (1) follows from the explicit product-dual pairing and naturality of evaluation. Part (2): the restriction map $\widehat G\to\widehat H$ is (by construction) the transpose of the inclusion and commutes with evaluation; the pullback of the quotient map is the transpose of the quotient and commutes with evaluation; both identifications of duals are the ones already proved on this page, so the diagrams commute and the double annihilator statement is [[lem-annihilator-reverses-inclusion-and-double-annihilator-closes]]. Part (3) is the same computation on finite products using (1) and coordinatewise restriction.

items.title: Dualisation is a contravariant involution
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $\varphi:G\to H$ be a continuous homomorphism of locally compact Hausdorff abelian groups. Then $\widehat\varphi:\widehat H\to\widehat G$, $\widehat\varphi(\gamma):=\gamma\circ\varphi$, is a continuous homomorphism, $\widehat{\operatorname{id}_G}=\operatorname{id}_{\widehat G}$, and for composable $\varphi,\psi$ one has $\widehat{\psi\circ\varphi}=\widehat\varphi\circ\widehat\psi$; thus $(-)^\wedge$ is a contravariant functor into locally compact Hausdorff abelian groups. Moreover the evaluation maps are natural, $$\Phi_H\circ\varphi=\widehat{\widehat\varphi}\circ\Phi_G,$$ so that $\Phi$ is a natural isomorphism from the identity functor to the double-dual functor; dualisation is therefore a contravariant involution of the category of locally compact Hausdorff abelian groups, and it preserves finite products, closed subgroups and quotients in the sense of [[lem-biduality-is-stable-under-products-closed-subgroups-and-quotients]].

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, Theorems C.12-C.13 and the homomorphism-dual paragraph following C.13, printed p. 437: evaluation biduality and contravariant pullback. Naturality is computed here.

items.strategy: Continuity and multiplicativity of $\widehat\varphi$ are the published functoriality of duals ([[lem-dual-homomorphisms-are-continuous-and-functorial]]), and the composition law is a direct computation on values: $\widehat{\psi\circ\varphi}(\gamma)=\gamma\circ\psi\circ\varphi=\widehat\varphi(\widehat\psi(\gamma))$. Naturality of $\Phi$ is also a direct evaluation computation: for $x\in G$ and $\gamma\in\widehat H$ one has $\Phi_H(\varphi(x))(\gamma)=\gamma(\varphi(x))=\widehat{\widehat\varphi}(\Phi_G(x))(\gamma)$. That $\Phi$ is an isomorphism in every degree is [[thm-pontryagin-biduality]].

items.title: Totally disconnected LCA groups have bases of compact open subgroups

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Lemmas 14.9 and 14.10, printed p. 28: compact open sets and compact open subgroup neighbourhoods in totally disconnected locally compact groups.

items.strategy: A totally disconnected locally compact Hausdorff space has a basis of compact open sets, so every neighbourhood of 0 contains a compact open set E0; enlarge to a compact open E with 0∈E. (i) The set D:={(x,y): x∈E, x+y∉E} is closed in E×G and misses E×{0}; compactness of E and the tube lemma give a neighbourhood W0 of 0 with E+W0⊆E; replacing W0 by W0∩(−W0) gives W=−W and E+W=E (as E⊆E+W). (ii) Put F:={x∈G: x+E=E}; then F is a subgroup (closure of the condition under addition and inversion), F⊆E (x∈x+E=E), F⊇W (x∈W gives x+E=E+W=E), so F is open, and F is closed because {x: x+E⊆E} and {x: E⊆x+E} are intersections of the closed sets E−e and e−E over e∈E. Being closed in the compact E, F is compact; thus F is a compact open subgroup of G contained in E. (iii) Since F is open, the cosets of F partition E into open sets and compactness of E gives a finite subcover. Applying this in each neighbourhood of 0 yields the claimed basis.

items.title: Every LCA group has an open compactly generated subgroup with no open subgroup of infinite index
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian topological group ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]], [[def-topological-group]]). Then $G$ contains an open (hence closed) subgroup $H$ which is compactly generated and contains no open subgroup of infinite index. For instance, if $G$ is discrete one may take $H=\{0\}$.

references.title: K. A. Ross, Closed subgroups of compactly generated LCA groups are compactly generated (author-hosted article, 2018)
references.locator: Theorem 3 proof, printed p. 3: quotes the decomposition into a Euclidean factor, a finitely generated free discrete factor, and a compact abelian factor, citing Hewitt-Ross Theorem 9.8.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Lemma 14.13, printed p. 29: the open compactly generated subgroup with no open subgroup of infinite index.

items.strategy: Choose a compact symmetric identity neighbourhood $C$ whose interior contains the identity, and let $H_0:=\langle C\rangle=\bigcup_{k\ge1}C^k$. Then $H_0$ is open and compactly generated. By the compactly generated LCA structure theorem (Hewitt--Ross, Theorem 9.8), choose a topological isomorphism $H_0\cong\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb Z^n\times K$ with $K$ compact. The preimage $H$ of $\mathbb R^m\times\{0\}\times K$ is open in $H_0$, hence in $G$, and compactly generated (a compact ball in $\mathbb R^m$ times $K$ generates it). If $L\le H$ is open, then $H/L$ is discrete. The image of the connected factor $\mathbb R^m$ in this discrete quotient is trivial, so $\mathbb R^m\le L$. Thus $H/L$ is a discrete quotient of compact $K$, hence finite. Therefore $H$ has no open subgroup of infinite index.

items.title: A compactly generated LCA group with no open subgroup of infinite index is Euclidean times compact
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $H$ be a compactly generated locally compact Hausdorff abelian topological group ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]], [[def-topological-group]], [[def-generated-subgroup]]) containing no open subgroup of infinite index. Then there are $n\ge0$ and a compact group $W$ with $H\cong W\oplus\mathbb R^n$ (topological group isomorphism), the summands being the direct factors of the product $W\times\mathbb R^n$.

references.title: K. A. Ross, Closed subgroups of compactly generated LCA groups are compactly generated (author-hosted article, 2018)
references.locator: Theorem 3 proof, printed p. 3: the compactly generated LCA classification attributed to Hewitt-Ross Theorem 9.8; elimination of the discrete factor is proved here.

items.strategy: Apply the compactly generated LCA structure theorem (Hewitt--Ross, Theorem 9.8): $H\cong\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb Z^n\times K$ for a compact group $K$. If $n>0$, then $\mathbb R^m\times\{0\}\times K$ is an open subgroup of infinite index, contradicting the hypothesis. Hence $n=0$ and $H\cong\mathbb R^m\times K$, as claimed. This argument uses the cited classification directly; no compact-open decomposition prerequisite is needed.

items.title: The principal structure theorem for LCA groups
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian topological group ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]], [[def-topological-group]]). Then $G$ contains an open (hence closed) subgroup isomorphic as a topological group to $\mathbb R^n\times W$ for some $n\ge0$ and some compact group $W$.

references.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes)
references.locator: Theorem 14.6, printed p. 28, and Lemmas 14.13-14.14, printed p. 29: the principal structure theorem and its two reductions.

references.title: K. A. Ross, Closed subgroups of compactly generated LCA groups are compactly generated (author-hosted article, 2018)
references.locator: Theorem 3 proof, printed p. 3: quotes the compactly generated LCA classification used in the local reductions.

items.strategy: Apply [[lem-lca-group-has-an-open-compactly-generated-subgroup-with-no-open-subgroup-of-infinite-index]] to $G$ and obtain an open subgroup $H$ that is compactly generated and has no open subgroup of infinite index. Apply [[lem-compactly-generated-lca-group-with-no-open-subgroup-of-infinite-index-splits-as-compact-times-euclidean]] to $H$ to get $H\cong\mathbb R^n\times K$ for a compact group $K$. This is the desired open subgroup. The compactly generated classification used in both local lemmas is Hewitt--Ross, Theorem 9.8; K. A. Ross, Theorem 3 proof, p. 3, records the exact theorem statement and attribution.

title: Pontryagin Duality for Locally Compact Abelian Groups — Examples

items.title: Annihilators of closed subgroups of Euclidean space
items.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ and $0\le k\le n$ be integers. Coordinates are indexed by $0\le i<n$ ([[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]]). Work in $G=\mathbb R^n$ with the dual identified with $\mathbb R^n$ by $\xi\mapsto(x\mapsto e^{2\pi i\,\xi\cdot x})$, computed below from the classification of characters of the line and the product-dual identification ([[lem-continuous-characters-of-the-real-line-are-exponentials]], [[lem-duals-of-finite-products-and-discrete-direct-sums]]). No choice principle is used by the computations below; the general quotient-dual and closed-subgroup identifications cited in the dependency list give the context of clause (2), whose coordinate content is computed directly here.

(1) If $V\le\mathbb R^n$ is a linear subspace, then $V^\perp=\{\xi:\xi\cdot v\in\mathbb Z\ \text{for all}\ v\in V\}$; when $V=\mathbb R^k\times\{0\}^{n-k}$ this is $\{0\}^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}$, the coarse orthogonal complement, whereas for the lattice $H=\mathbb Z^k\times\{0\}^{n-k}$ it is $\mathbb Z^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}$. For $k=n$ the annihilator of the full-rank lattice $\mathbb Z^n$ is again the lattice $\mathbb Z^n$, while for $k<n$ the annihilator contains the line $\mathbb R\,e_k$ and is not discrete; so an annihilator is not in general an orthogonal complement.

(2) For $H=\mathbb Z^k\times\{0\}^{n-k}$ the quotient $\mathbb R^n/H$ is identified with $(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}$, and its characters are computed on the standard coordinates by the discrete Fourier pairing: its characters are exactly the maps $x+H\mapsto e^{2\pi i\,\xi\cdot x}$ with $\xi\in\mathbb Z^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}$, whose pullbacks are precisely the characters of $\mathbb R^n$ trivial on $H$.

(3) If $A$ is an invertible $n\times n$ real matrix and $H=A\mathbb Z^n$, then $H^\perp=A^{-T}\mathbb Z^n$ with $A^{-T}:=(A^{-1})^T=(A^T)^{-1}$.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Sections 35A-35C, printed pp. 138-140: finite products, quotient duals and the topological real-line dual. The annihilator formulas are computed here.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, Example C.14(2), printed p. 438: exponential parametrisation of real-line characters.

items.strategy: Real-character classification and finite-product duality identify exponential parameters. The topology on the line is checked in both directions using bounded compact sets and the half-period test. Triviality on H is exactly xi·h in Z for every h. Coordinate and lattice tests give the displayed subspace/lattice annihilators; for A Z^n, the condition is A^T xi in Z^n, equivalently xi in A^−T Z^n. The finite product quotient map is open continuous with kernel H; quotient characters evaluate on x+H and pull back to the corresponding ambient characters. Empty dimension and rank endpoints are explicit.

items.title: The bidual map on the circle and the integers
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]); the two identifications of values below are direct computations from the classifications of the characters of $\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb T$ given in the Facts, and the continuity statement is exactly [[thm-pontryagin-biduality]]. Under the identifications $\widehat{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb T$, $z\mapsto(n\mapsto z^n)$, and $\widehat{\mathbb T}\cong\mathbb Z$, $k\mapsto(z\mapsto z^k)$, the evaluation map $\Phi_{\mathbb Z}:\mathbb Z\to\widehat{\widehat{\mathbb Z}}$ is the identity of $\mathbb Z$, and $\Phi_{\mathbb T}:\mathbb T\to\widehat{\widehat{\mathbb T}}$ is the identity of $\mathbb T$. In particular the abstract biduality identification is the natural one on these two groups, not merely an abstract isomorphism.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Sections 35D-35F, printed p. 140: the circle/integer duals and their concrete biduality.

references.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
references.locator: Appendix C.3, Theorem C.12, printed p. 437, and Example C.14(1), printed p. 438: evaluation biduality and integer characters.

items.strategy: Compute: for $n\in\mathbb Z$ and $z\in\mathbb T$, $\Phi_{\mathbb Z}(n)(z)=z^n$, which under $\widehat{\mathbb T}\cong\mathbb Z$ is the integer $n$. Likewise for $z\in\mathbb T$ and $k\in\mathbb Z=\widehat{\mathbb T}$ one has $\Phi_{\mathbb T}(z)(k)=z^k$, which under $\widehat{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb T$ is $z$. Continuity is [[thm-pontryagin-biduality]].

items.title: Forgetting the compact-open topology destroys Pontryagin duality
items.statement: The biduality conclusion of Pontryagin duality holds for every algebraic character group when the group is equipped with the discrete topology: if $X$ is the algebraic character group $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z,\mathbb T)$ of the discrete group $\mathbb Z$ with the discrete topology, then the evaluation map $\mathbb Z\to\operatorname{Hom}_{cts}(X,\mathbb T)$ is an isomorphism.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
references.locator: Sections 35D-35F, printed p. 140: the topological circle/integer duals used for comparison. The Hamel-coordinate counterexample is constructed here from the cited Hamel-basis supplier.

items.strategy: The specific Q-linear map T constructed from a Hamel basis sends Z into Z, so it induces a well-defined homomorphism f_T([t])=T(t)+Z. If f_T were continuous for the compact-open circle topology, it would be z↦z^k for some integer k. Then D(t)=T(t)-kt is additive with image in Z, so D(t)=nD(t/n) lies in nZ for every n and therefore D=0, forcing T=kI contrary to the chosen basis values. On the discrete X, f_T is continuous and lies outside the evaluation image.
